about.title: Is the name-guess baseline really that good?
about.note: Curated subset of the artifact's shipped output. The primary demo dataset is arm1_edited_positives (84 measured edited checkpoints). The other blocks are the compact reference rows the arm-1 de-biasing, the arm-3 false-positive rate and the arm-2 paired comparison are computed from.

verdicts.ARM1_is_the_regex_baseline_inflated: PARTLY. Measured on the name-free discovery channel the repo-name regex catches 0.642 [0.507, 0.757] of self-declared edited checkpoints (n=53), against 0.953 [0.925, 0.970] (n=358) on the checkpoints the abliteration-vocabulary search sweeps found. The gap is the selection effect. The archived 0.727 DOES lie inside the de-biased interval, so 0.727 survives as an estimate -- but it is an estimate of a much weaker baseline than the 0.95 the term-swept pool would suggest.
verdicts.ARM1_does_W05_see_what_the_regex_cannot: NO, on this evidence. Across 84 measured edited checkpoints, W05 fires on 10/50 of those the regex already names and on 0/34 of those it does not (95% upper bound 0.102). At the LORCO refit threshold the undeclared cell is still 1/34. The set caught-by-W05-missed-by-name is EMPTY at the panel threshold and holds 1 rows at the refit threshold (KnutJaegersberg/Walter-Falcon-1B). That is the single most consequential result in this artifact: on ordinary Hub traffic the weights-only detector adds at most a handful of rows the repo name did not already give away, and at the calibrated panel threshold it adds none.
verdicts.ARM2_are_the_card_labels_real: NOT ALL OF THEM. Of 12 behaviourally assessable card-labelled positives, 4 verify as un-censored and 3 still refuse at least 80% of the frozen harmful core (0.250 [0.089, 0.532]). So the 44-row positive-class denominator is itself uncertain, and the sensitivity is reported as an interval over denominators. Only 4 of the 14 subsampled rows reach VERIFIED_UNCENSORED, below the pre-set floor of 6, so the sensitivity restricted to verified rows is not estimable. What IS estimable is the reliability of the card label itself, reported in card_label_reliability.
verdicts.ARM2_head_to_head_on_verified_rows: The regex beats W05 on the subsample: paired difference 0.6153846153846154 [0.3076923076923077, 0.8461538461538463] over 13 rows, an interval that excludes zero.
verdicts.ARM3_does_specificity_hold_on_chat_model: AT THE PANEL THRESHOLD, YES; AT THE REFIT THRESHOLD, NO. On 251 eligible undeclared checkpoints (159 chat / 78 base) the false-positive rate at TAU_PANEL is 0/251 pooled and 0/159 on the chat subset (95% upper bound 0.024). At TAU_REFIT it is 0.080 pooled, 0.044 chat and 0.154 base. The refit threshold, which has never been reported before, therefore costs real specificity, and it costs it disproportionately on BASE models. The closest negative sits at W05 = -2.6139, 0.1276 log10 units from TAU_PANEL.
verdicts.OVERALL: The reviewer's objection stands up to measurement and then partly reverses. The 0.727 name baseline IS inflated by the discovery channel -- 0.953 on term-swept rows against 0.642 on name-free ones -- but de-biasing it does not rescue the weights-only detector. On the 34 edited checkpoints the regex cannot see, W05 fires 0 times at the calibrated panel threshold and 1 at the refit threshold; its specificity is intact only at the panel threshold (0/251 vs 20/251); and a quarter of the card-labelled positives it is scored against do not behave as un-censored at all. The honest summary is that at the one threshold where the detector is trustworthy it finds nothing the repo name did not, and at the threshold where it starts finding things it also starts firing on unedited base models.
